external_entities.name: developers
external_entities.description: People who push branches to the self-hosted git server and can log in to the build runner.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server
external_entities.notes: The text does not state where the developers are located or what trust zone they occupy.

external_entities.name: public package registry
external_entities.description: The public package registry reached during dependency resolution.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet

processes.name: build runner
processes.description: Picks up merges, fetches source, resolves the dependency lockfile, produces container images, pushes images to the registry, calls the deploy controller, and permits developers to initiate rebuilds.
processes.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source, resolves the dependency lockfile and produces a container image.
processes.notes: A shared build token is used when calling the deploy controller. The runner does not verify signatures on downloads.

processes.name: deploy controller
processes.description: Maintains the current release selected for the estate and answers release queries from store servers.
processes.source_excerpt: The deploy controller runs on the corporate network and holds one record: which image sha the estate should be on.

processes.name: store server
processes.description: A small server in each store's back office that polls the deploy controller, pulls a changed image, and restarts the container.
processes.source_excerpt: Every store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is
processes.notes: There are about 1,200 stores, each with a small server.

processes.name: till software
processes.description: The till software running as a container on each store server.
processes.source_excerpt: running the till software as a container

data_stores.name: git server
data_stores.description: The self-hosted git server containing developer branches and the source used for builds.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server
data_stores.notes: Nobody has documented whether the git server encrypts what it stores.

data_stores.name: image registry
data_stores.description: The registry storing finished container images tagged with commit shas.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry
data_stores.notes: Nobody has documented whether the image registry encrypts what it stores. The registry allows store-server pulls.

data_stores.name: current release record
data_stores.description: The record identifying which image sha the estate should be running.
data_stores.source_excerpt: holds one record: which image sha the estate should be on
data_stores.notes: The record is held by the deploy controller, but the text does not separately place this data store in a network zone.

data_flows.name: push branches
data_flows.description: Developers push branches to the self-hosted git server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server

data_flows.name: start build
data_flows.description: A merge to main starts a build on the build runner.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A merge to `main` is what starts a build.

data_flows.name: fetch source
data_flows.description: The build runner fetches source from the git server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source

data_flows.name: publish image
data_flows.description: The build runner pushes the finished container image to the image registry.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry
data_flows.notes: Images are tagged with the commit sha.
data_flows.data_description: finished container image tagged with the commit sha

data_flows.name: set release
data_flows.description: The build runner calls the deploy controller and asks it to make an image the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When the image is pushed the runner calls the deploy controller and asks it to make that image the current release.
data_flows.notes: The runner uses a shared build token that is the same for every pipeline and has not been rotated since the pipeline was set up.

data_flows.name: read release
data_flows.description: Each store server asks the deploy controller for the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is
data_flows.notes: Nobody has written down what a store server presents to the controller.

data_flows.name: pull image
data_flows.description: A store server pulls the current image from the registry when its running image differs.
data_flows.source_excerpt: if it differs from what it is running it pulls that image from the registry
data_flows.notes: The registry allows the pull; nobody has written down what a store server presents to it.
data_flows.data_description: container image tagged with the commit sha

data_flows.name: resolve dependencies
data_flows.description: The build runner reaches out to the public package registry while resolving dependencies.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet
data_flows.notes: The runner does not verify signatures on what it downloads.

data_flows.name: kick rebuild
data_flows.description: A developer logs in to the build runner and manually starts a rebuild of main.
data_flows.source_excerpt: any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of `main` by hand
data_flows.notes: This path does not require a merge and is not reviewed.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network zone containing the self-hosted git server and deploy controller.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: which sits on the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: build environment
trust_boundaries.description: The separate build environment containing the build runner and image registry.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The runner lives in its own build environment, separate from the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: store estate
trust_boundaries.description: The store-side zone containing the store servers and till software containers.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The image registry is reachable from the store estate over the WAN.

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: The public internet zone reached by dependency resolution.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the public package registry on the internet

assumptions.assumption: The git server's source code and branches are confidential because they are business-sensitive build inputs.
assumptions.basis: The store contains developer branches and source code used to build the till software.

assumptions.assumption: The image registry's container images are confidential because they are business-sensitive software artifacts.
assumptions.basis: The store contains finished container images deployed to the store estate.

assumptions.assumption: The current release record is internal because it is an operational record used inside the organisation to identify the estate's release.
assumptions.basis: The record contains which image sha the estate should be running and is used by the internal deploy controller and store servers.
